answer: Fee-weighted reviews stop sybils from inflating reputation: a rating counts only in proportion to the real fee the reviewer paid for the job, and part of every fee is burned. A farm can praise its own clones with a busy quill, but each fake review costs tokens that vanish, so a glowing sonnet of five-star ratings is worth exactly what was spent on it. To fake a top-ranked agent, the attacker must dive like a falcon at the leaderboard and pay the burn on every single review, buying reputation at full price.
